correctness.rationale: The exact common-neighbor complement is S union (S+1), with size |S|+number of cyclic runs. This gives the face lists at t=3,4,5. At t=4 all n triangles have unique length-two free edges, so collapse yields a graph with cycle rank binom(n,2)-2n+1. At t=5 the only tetrahedra are n consecutive runs; their n distinct free triangular faces collapse to a simply-connected 2-complex. The f-vector (n,binom(n,2),n(n-3),n) yields H_2(Z)=Z^[n(n-5)/2-1]; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead prove the integral wedge, with no higher homology. The cyclic cycle remains primitive at t=4 and bounds at t=5. The embedded independent adjacency-based checker verifies f-vectors and mod-2 boundary ranks for n=7..11, plus free-face uniqueness and inclusion cycle status; no finite-to-infinite inference is used.

value.rationale: The graph is the canonical complete bipartite network after deleting a Hamiltonian 2-factor, and witness count is the natural filtration density parameter introduced by the 2023 source. The first three positive nontrivial coverage cutoffs are determined structurally by two deleted neighbors per vertex, not arbitrary small slices. The theorem captures a sharp circle-to-quadratic-circle-to-2-sphere transition and primitive/zero inclusion maps uniformly for every n>=7, which cannot be inferred from raw combinatorial correctness alone. The result is limited to a motivated finite window, not advertised as the full barcode.
